Here’s an advanced Keras + Spektral project using temporal Graph Neural Networks for multivariate time‑series forecasting—a major leap beyond typical CNN/RNN tasks:

🧠 Project Title

ai‑ml‑ds‑JfV9kLpXzNf – Temporal Graph Neural Network for Multivariate Time‑Series Forecasting
Filename: temporal_graph_forecasting_spektral.py

🔍 Short Description

Build and train a Temporal Graph Neural Network (TGNN) in Keras using Spektral to forecast multiple time‑series that have inter-node dependencies. You’ll use a dynamic graph where node features are time‑series observations and the adjacency describes inter-series correlation. This project fuses temporal (TCN) and graph (GAT) layers.

# temporal_graph_forecasting_spektral.py

import numpy as np  # type: np.ndarray
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras import Input, Model
from tensorflow.keras.layers import Dense, Conv1D, Dropout
from spektral.layers import GraphAttention, GlobalSumPool
from spektral.data import Dataset, Graph
from spektral.data.loaders import DisjointLoader
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

# 1. Generate synthetic multivariate time-series data
num_series: int = 10
total_time: int = 1000
window: int = 12
horizon: int = 3

rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
data: np.ndarray = rng.randn(total_time, num_series)

# 2. Create adjacency via correlation
corr: np.ndarray = np.corrcoef(data.T)
A: np.ndarray = (np.abs(corr) > 0.5).astype('float32')
np.fill_diagonal(A, 0.0)

# 3. Build samples
X_list, y_list, A_list = [], [], []
for t in range(total_time - window - horizon):
    x: np.ndarray = data[t:t+window]           # shape (window, num_series)
    y: np.ndarray = data[t+window:t+window+horizon]
    X_list.append(x)
    y_list.append(y)
    A_list.append(A)

X_arr: np.ndarray = np.stack(X_list)
y_arr: np.ndarray = np.stack(y_list)
A_arr: np.ndarray = np.stack(A_list)

# 4. Train/test split
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test, A_train, A_test = train_test_split(
    X_arr, y_arr, A_arr, test_size=0.2, random_state=1
)

# 5. Create Spektral Dataset
class TimeSeriesGraphDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, X, y, A, **kwargs):
        self.X, self.y, self.A = X, y, A
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
    def read(self):
        data = []
        for i in range(len(self.X)):
            x_i = self.X[i]  # (window, num_series)
            x_flat = x_i.T   # (num_series, window)
            data.append(Graph(x=x_flat, a=self.A[i], y=self.y[i]))
        return data

ds_train = TimeSeriesGraphDataset(X_train, y_train, A_train)
ds_test = TimeSeriesGraphDataset(X_test, y_test, A_test)
loader_tr = DisjointLoader(ds_train, batch_size=32, epochs=10)
loader_te = DisjointLoader(ds_test, batch_size=32)

# 6. Model definition
N: int = num_series
F: int = window
HIDDEN: int = 64
OUT_STEP: int = horizon

X_in = Input(shape=(F,), name="X_in")
A_in = Input(shape=(None,), sparse=True, name="A_in")
fl = GraphAttention(channels=HIDDEN, activation="elu")([X_in, A_in])
tl = tf.expand_dims(fl, -1)
tl = Conv1D(32, kernel_size=3, activation='relu')(tl)
tl = tf.squeeze(tl, -1)
pl = GlobalSumPool()(tl)
dl = Dense(OUT_STEP * N)(pl)
out = tf.reshape(dl, (-1, OUT_STEP, N))
model = Model(inputs=[X_in, A_in], outputs=out)
model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='mse')
model.summary()

# 7. Training & evaluation
model.fit(loader_tr.load(), steps_per_epoch=loader_tr.steps_per_epoch, epochs=20)
print("Test MSE:", model.evaluate(loader_te.load(), steps=loader_te.steps_per_epoch))

# 8. Usage example: single sample
x0: np.ndarray = X_test[0]  # (window, num_series)
a0: np.ndarray = A_test[0]
x0_graph = Graph(x=x0.T, a=a0)
pred0: np.ndarray = model.predict(loader_te.load().__next__())[0]
print("Predicted shape:", pred0.shape)
print("Predicted sample:", pred0)

✅ Example I/O

  • Input: 12 time-steps for 10 correlated series
  • Output: Next 3 time-steps predicted for each series
Predicted shape: (3, 10)
Predicted sample: [[...], [...], [...]]

🧩 Key Learnings & Research Areas

  • Spektral, Keras integration with graph layers
  • GraphAttention, GlobalSumPool, Conv1D for temporal modeling
  • Topics: dynamic graph forecasting, multivariate time-series, spectral vs. spatial attention
  • Tags/googleables: Spektral, Temporal GNN, GraphAttention, Spatio-Temporal Forecasting, Time-Series Graphs, Spektral Keras, GNN Time Series

🌍 Problem Domain & Use Cases

  • Domain: Forecasting multivariate signals with inter-series correlation
  • Use Cases: Traffic load forecasts at sensors, multi-location energy demand, disease surveillance networks, IoT multi-sensor prediction

🛠 Frameworks Used

  • Spektral (GNN layers in Keras/TensorFlow) (graphneural.network, arxiv.org, ijcai.org, github.com)
  • Keras (Conv1D) for temporal features

📈 Development Lifecycle (Corp Perspective)

  1. Requirement gathering, stakeholder alignment
  2. Data ingestion pipeline, synthetic validation
  3. Prototyping on synthetic data
  4. Refinement with real datasets (e.g. UCI traffic)
  5. Performance & stress testing, deployment
  6. Monitoring forecasting drift, continuous retraining

🤝 Sister Projects & Integrations

  • Sister: Spektral-based static GNN for classification/regression
  • Integrate with: Airflow for pipelined forecasting, Prometheus for monitoring, FastAPI serving predictions

⏰ Timestamp

2025‑07‑15

Estimated duration: 4–6 weeks to production-ready solution

📦 Final Product

A deployable TGNN forecasting pipeline with automated retraining on shifts, visualization dashboard, and alerting on anomalies.

🚀 Pro-Level Challenge

  • Swap adjacency to dynamic: recalculating A from rolling correlations
  • Add uncertainty via Monte Carlo dropout, forecasting intervals
  • Replace Conv1D with TCN or Transformer layers for deeper temporal processing
  • Benchmark against StemGNN, A3T‑GCN (github.com, arxiv.org)

🌟 Where to Go From Here

  • Scale to heterogeneous node types (sensors+events)
  • Add edge features & encode into TGNN
  • Add explainability (GNNExplainer)
  • Explore real-world datasets: METR‑LA, PEMS‑Bay

This is a far more demanding and varied project than standard CNN/RNN tasks—you’re modeling dynamic graphs over time, fusing spectral and spatial dependencies with GNN layers.
